The available sources provide limited information regarding Norman Borlaug and the Green Revolution as historical events. The primary information available connects "Norman Borlaug's Green Revolution" to the concept of heterosis within the framework of the Van Kush Family Research Institute (VKFRI).

== Norman Borlaug and the Green Revolution ==
Within the context of a paper examining heterosis, selective breeding, and transgenerational epigenetic inheritance, "Norman Borlaug's Green Revolution" is cited as a "heterosis demonstration" <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>. The available sources do not specify the historical details of Norman Borlaug's life, his specific contributions, or the broader historical context, goals, or outcomes of the Green Revolution.

== Connection to Heterosis ==
The paper "Depicting the heterosis mechanism through selective breeding, epigenetic inheritance, and the mechanics of genetic recombination across domesticated species" uses "Norman Borlaug's Green Revolution" as an example of a heterosis demonstration <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>.

[[Heterosis]], also known as hybrid vigor, is examined as one of several interconnected phenomena, alongside selective breeding and transgenerational epigenetic inheritance <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>. These phenomena are presented as illuminating the mechanics of genetic recombination across domesticated species <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>.

== Related Concepts ==
The VKFRI paper discusses several concepts relevant to the understanding of the Green Revolution as a heterosis demonstration:
*   **Selective Breeding**: This process is examined in conjunction with heterosis and transgenerational epigenetic inheritance <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>.
*   **Epigenetic Inheritance**: This refers to heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the underlying DNA sequence <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>. It is discussed as an interconnected phenomenon with heterosis and selective breeding <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>.
*   **Genetic Recombination**: The paper explores how heterosis, selective breeding, and epigenetic inheritance illuminate the mechanics of genetic recombination across various domesticated species <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>.

== Van Kush Framework ==
The paper introduces the Van Kush Framework, which proposes that epigenetic inheritance, instinctual behavior, and genetic recombination together form a natural system <ref>knowledge/scripture/heterosis_mechanism.md</ref>.
